newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh court grants bail to ex-PM Zia's son.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh court grants bail to ex-PM Zia's son.

text.p: Bangladesh's High Court on Monday granted "anticipatory bail" for two months to former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia's son and brother, who currently face corruption charges, court officials said.
The bail, granted after two days of hearing, will prevent police from arresting Khaleda's son Tareq Rahman and brother Syeed Iskander until November 23.

Under Bangladesh law, anticipatory bail can be sought to forestall anticipated police action. Otherwise, the authorities have the power to detain a person for up to four months pending trial or even before being formally charged.
Hundreds of leaders and activists of Khaleda's opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) crowded the court room during the hearing.
Many others gathered outside in what witnesses said was a show of support for Khaleda's next to kins being embroiled in defamatory court proceedings.

Bangladesh's Anti-Corruption Bureau filed charges against Tareq Rahman and his uncle Syeed Iskander on September 16, saying they overvalued land used as partial collateral when borrowing 153 million taka ($3.8 million) from the state-owned Sonali Bank to set up a textile dyeing company.
Police said the accused put a value 1.8 million taka on land worth only 120,000 taka.
Rahman and Iskander applied on Wednesday for anticipatory bail. The first hearing took place on Sunday.
Chief government lawyer K. S. Nabi opposed the bail, saying that the accused were charged with irregularities with public money.
Moudud Ahmed, lawyer for Rahman and Iskander, said he had argued that the "case was of civil nature and could not be treated as a criminal case."
